Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: SARB’s Vision 2025 for the National Payment System explicitly includes financial inclusion objectives (e.g., broaden access and reduce reliance on cash) and references collaborative governance with industry bodies like PASA/BankservAfrica rather than a dedicated pro-poor governance body ([South African Reserve Bank – Vision 2025](https://www.resbank.co.za/en/home/what-we-do/national-payment-system/overview/vision-2025)).  This indicates inclusion is a formal objective, but governance mechanisms specific to pro-poor representation are limited/indirect.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: PayShap participation/product rules are not fully published as a single publicly accessible “scheme rulebook”; instead, consumer-facing rules and usage conditions are mainly available via bank-specific PayShap terms and conditions (e.g., Standard Bank PayShap T&Cs describing ShapID registration and transaction rules) ([Standard Bank](https://www.standardbank.co.za/southafrica/personal/products-and-services/digital-banking/ways-to-bank/standard-bank-app/payshap/terms-and-conditions)).  Public information about PayShap exists on SARB/BankservAfrica pages, but comprehensive scheme rules for all participants are not clearly available openly.

Definition: Whether refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, migrants, and stateless persons can legally access and open digital payment accounts, and practical barriers or enablers for these populations.
Comments: Refugees and asylum seekers in South Africa can access at least some government digital payment programs: UNHCR South Africa’s guidance on the SASSA SRD grant states eligibility includes “Refugee registered on the Home Affairs database” and “an asylum seeker whose section 22 permit… is valid,” and applicants can use a DHA refugee/asylum permit number, indicating documented access pathways with valid documentation ([UNHCR South Africa](https://help.unhcr.org/southafrica/2022/02/21/sassa-srd-r350-grant/)).  However, access is tied to legal status and documentation, and broader payment inclusion for undocumented migrants is not clearly supported in official sources, suggesting partial inclusion.
